summary: Go ToolSearch has a working deferred-tool discovery loop, structured ToolReferenceBlock results, registry visibility filtering, dynamic MCP tool support, cache/index helpers, and several local tests. It is still not fully aligned with the TypeScript reference. The most important differences are that Go exposes a different input schema (`limit` instead of TS `max_results`), routes keyword searches through BM25/embedding behavior instead of the TS fixed keyword scorer and fast paths, lacks TS's per-request enablement gates and provider-specific defer_loading/beta handling, does not announce deferred-tool deltas during normal turns, and does not reliably preserve loaded deferred tools across compaction/resume. Some existing Go alignment tests encode non-TS expectations, so they currently protect divergences rather than parity.

gaps.title: Go exposes `limit` while TS exposes `max_results`
gaps.description: The TS input schema is `{ query: string, max_results?: number }` with a default of 5. Go's public schema advertises `limit`, min/max bounds, and no `max_results`; it only accepts `max_results` as a hidden legacy struct field. This changes the model-facing API and can make TS-compatible callers invisible to schema-driven prompting while making Go-generated `limit` calls invalid against the TS tool.

ts_evidence.note: TS declares `query` and optional `max_results` with default 5.

go_evidence.note: Go Schema() declares `query` and `limit`, with minimum/maximum bounds.
Execute reads `Limit`, falls back to `MaxResults`, defaults to 5, and clamps to [1, 50].
ToolSearchInput marks `Limit` as canonical and `MaxResults` as backwards compatibility.

gaps.impact: Schema-driven model/tool clients diverge from TS. Existing Go parity tests assert the opposite of the current TS reference.

gaps.title: Go Execute uses BM25/embedding ranking instead of TS keyword scorer and fast paths
gaps.description: TS keyword search has explicit behavior: bare exact tool name returns directly, `mcp__server` prefix returns prefix matches directly, `+term` filters candidates by name/description/searchHint, and scores with fixed weights over parsed name parts, searchHint, and prompt description. Go's Execute path builds a ToolIndex and BM25Ranker, optionally reranks embeddings, and never calls the preserved TS-like `searchToolsWithKeywords` helper. This loses TS fast paths; for example a bare CamelCase tool name can tokenize differently from the indexed expanded identifier.

ts_evidence.note: TS exact-name and `mcp__` prefix fast paths run before scoring.
TS partitions required terms and applies fixed score weights for name parts, hints, and descriptions.

go_evidence.note: Go keyword Execute path refreshes BM25 index/ranker, caches ScoredMatch results, and optionally embedding-reranks.
BM25 Rank() tokenizes/scales documents and sorts by BM25 score, not TS fixed weights.
A TS-like searchToolsWithKeywords helper still exists but is marked legacy and is not used by Execute.

gaps.impact: Search result ordering and even match/no-match behavior can differ for exact names, MCP prefixes, required terms, stopwords, and CamelCase names.

gaps.title: Go result shape and model-facing prompt differ from TS
gaps.description: TS declares a typed output object with `matches`, `query`, `total_deferred_tools`, and optional `pending_mcp_servers`, then maps successful results to pure `tool_reference` content blocks. Go returns a ToolResult with prose summaries, optional metadata (`scores`, `rerank`, MCP state strings), and ToolReferenceBlocks; its prompt describes BM25 scores/snippets rather than the TS deferred-tool-location and result-format contract. On empty results, TS emits the fixed text `No matching deferred tools found` plus a pending-server sentence only when applicable; Go includes query text, deferred pool count, missing names, and richer MCP-state prose/metadata.

ts_evidence.note: TS outputSchema is the typed matches/query/total_deferred_tools/pending_mcp_servers object.
TS maps success to tool_reference blocks and empty results to a short fixed text response.
TS prompt explains deferred-tool locations, complete schema availability, result format, and query forms.

go_evidence.note: Go description advertises BM25 ranking, snippets, and numeric rank scores.
Go buildToolSearchResult renders prose summaries, ToolReferenceBlocks, scores metadata, rerank metadata, and MCP-state metadata.
Go's generic ToolResult has string Content, ContentBlocks, and string metadata rather than the TS output schema object.

gaps.impact: Downstream consumers and model-visible instructions do not see the same contract as TS; existing Go-only metadata and wording are not TS-compatible.

gaps.title: ToolSearch enablement is static in Go instead of TS per-request gating
gaps.description: TS has an optimistic base-tool inclusion check, then a definitive per-request `isToolSearchEnabled` check that considers environment mode, experimental beta kill switch, provider/proxy support, model support, ToolSearch availability after permissions/disallowed filtering, and auto-threshold sizing. It also disables ToolSearch for a request when there are no deferred tools and no pending MCP servers. Go registers ToolSearch once during SetupRegistry from a simplified env check and Registry.VisibleTools hides deferred tools whenever ToolSearch is registered, with no model, provider, permission/disallowed, auto-threshold, or no-deferred/pending request gate.

ts_evidence.note: TS getToolSearchMode implements true/false/auto modes and the experimental beta kill switch.
TS optimistic check disables default tool search for unsupported first-party proxy base URLs unless explicitly configured.
TS definitive check gates by model support, ToolSearch availability, mode, and auto threshold.
TS performs request-time filtering and disables ToolSearch when there are no deferred tools and no pending MCP servers.

go_evidence.note: Go optimistic check only evaluates env values and beta kill switch.
ToolSearch is registered once during registry setup.
VisibleTools hides deferred tools whenever ToolSearch is registered and loaded map lacks the tool.
Provider params use q.visibleToolDefinitions without a model/provider-specific ToolSearch enablement decision.

gaps.impact: Go can hide tools or emit tool_reference flows in sessions where TS would disable ToolSearch, and can keep ToolSearch visible when TS would filter it out.

gaps.title: Provider `defer_loading`, beta headers, and stale tool_reference stripping are not TS-equivalent
gaps.description: TS adds provider-specific tool-search beta headers only when request-time ToolSearch is enabled, marks deferred tool schemas with `defer_loading`, and strips tool_reference blocks when tool search is disabled or a referenced tool is no longer available. Go ToolDefinition has no `defer_loading` field, Anthropic beta header logic is hard-coded to the 1P header from env rather than the request's provider/model gate, and Anthropic conversion serializes ToolReferenceBlocks unconditionally whenever they exist.

ts_evidence.note: TS adds the provider-appropriate ToolSearch beta header only when useToolSearch is true.
TS passes deferLoading into toolToAPISchema while building tool schemas.
TS API tool schema supports `defer_loading` as a beta extra.
TS adds defer_loading when requested.
TS chooses advanced-tool-use for firstParty/foundry and tool-search-tool for Vertex/Bedrock.
TS strips tool_reference blocks when request-time tool search is disabled.
TS strips tool_reference blocks that point to unavailable tools.

go_evidence.note: Go ToolDefinition only has name, description, and input_schema.
Go adds a hard-coded 1P beta header based on env, without provider-specific header selection or model support checks.
Go converts every ToolReferenceBlock to an Anthropic tool_reference block unconditionally.
OpenAI fallback converts tool references to text markers rather than TS-style stripping/filtering logic.
Responses API fallback also converts tool references to text markers.

gaps.impact: Go can send beta-only content without the TS safety gates, cannot represent TS defer_loading on tool schemas, and can retain stale references that TS would remove before provider submission.

gaps.title: Go lacks TS per-turn deferred-tools delta announcements
gaps.description: TS announces deferred tools during normal attachment generation via `deferred_tools_delta` system reminders, or falls back to prepending an `<available-deferred-tools>` message when the delta gate is off. Go only has a post-compaction deferred-tools reminder; there is no normal-turn ToolSearch attachment in providerParams or loop attachment injection. That means the model may not see the TS-equivalent list of deferred tool names before it decides whether to use `select:<name>`.

ts_evidence.note: TS normal attachment generation includes deferred_tools_delta for main and subagent turns.
TS builds deferred_tools_delta after checking optimistic enablement, model support, and ToolSearch availability.
TS renders the delta as a system reminder listing available/removed deferred tools.
TS falls back to prepending `<available-deferred-tools>` when delta attachments are disabled.

go_evidence.note: Go provider params prepare messages/tools/system blocks but do not inject a deferred-tools announcement.
Go exposes deferred and loaded tool names only through post-compact attachment provider callbacks.
Go renders `Post-compaction deferred tools`, not a per-turn `deferred_tools_delta` equivalent.

gaps.impact: The model has weaker name discovery than TS and may rely on keyword search when TS would allow exact select based on announced names.

gaps.title: Loaded deferred tools are not reliably preserved across compaction and resume
gaps.description: TS reconstructs discovered tools by scanning nested tool_reference blocks inside tool_result content and by reading `preCompactDiscoveredTools` from compact boundary metadata. Go's live loop learns nested ToolReferenceBlocks from tool results during the current run, but compaction metadata extraction scans only top-level message blocks, so it misses the actual nested ToolSearch result shape. Repository search also shows no QueryLoop constructor/resume path that rebuilds `loadedToolNames` from existing messages or compact boundary metadata.

ts_evidence.note: TS extractDiscoveredToolNames reads compact boundary metadata and nested tool_reference blocks inside user tool_result content.
TS writes preCompactDiscoveredTools onto full compact boundaries.
TS also writes discovered tools for partial compaction using all messages.

go_evidence.note: Go learns loaded tools from nested ToolReferenceBlocks only in current tool results.
New QueryLoop initializes loadedToolNames as an empty map.
discoveredToolNames scans top-level ToolReferenceBlock and ToolUseBlock entries, not nested ToolResultBlock.ContentBlocks.
Compaction stores PreCompactDiscoveredTools using the incomplete discoveredToolNames helper.
Go can parse compact boundary metadata, but no loadedToolNames reconstruction path was found outside tests/event reporting.

gaps.impact: After compaction or session resume, previously loaded deferred tools can disappear from visible definitions even though TS would keep them loaded.

gaps.title: MCP pending-state and list_changed invalidation hooks exist but are not wired like TS runtime state
gaps.description: TS ToolSearch consults appState MCP clients on every empty result and reports pending server names. Go has global resolver hooks for pending/full MCP visibility state, and dynamic-MCP list_changed invalidator helpers, but repository search shows the resolver setters are only used by tests and SetupRegistry does not install list_changed invalidators for the production ToolSearch instance. As a result, empty ToolSearch misses normally omit TS pending_mcp_servers information, and dynamic MCP changes can rely on manual/test wiring rather than runtime wiring.

ts_evidence.note: TS reads pending MCP clients from getAppState().mcp.clients on each ToolSearch call.
TS includes pending server names when keyword search finds no matches.
TS includes pending server names when select finds no requested tools.

go_evidence.note: Go defines PendingMCPServersFn and MCPServerStatesFn globals.
Go formats current MCP visibility state only if the global resolver hooks return data.
Pending MCP coverage injects PendingMCPServersFn directly in a unit test.
SetupRegistry creates/refreshes MCP managers but does not wire ToolSearch pending-state resolvers or list_changed invalidators.
List_changed invalidator helper can clear ToolSearch, but repository search found production tests/calls only around explicit test registration.

gaps.impact: Go often loses TS's 'server still connecting' guidance and can serve stale ToolSearch indexes after MCP tool-list changes unless runtime code explicitly wires the helper.

gaps.title: Go lacks TS tool_reference message-normalization safeguards
gaps.description: TS has dedicated normalization for tool_reference blocks: strip all references when ToolSearch is disabled, strip references for unavailable tools, avoid mixing tool_reference with text inside a tool_result, and inject/relocate sibling text to avoid provider/model stop-sequence pathologies. Go serializes structured tool results directly to provider-specific formats and does not implement equivalent normalization before Anthropic/OpenAI/Responses conversion.

ts_evidence.note: TS strips tool_reference blocks when tool search is not enabled and inserts a placeholder when all content is stripped.
TS relocates text siblings away from tool_reference-containing user messages under the gate.
TS injects a separate text sibling boundary for tool_reference messages when relocation is disabled.
TS refuses to smoosh tool_reference content with other tool_result block types.

go_evidence.note: Go sends structured ToolResultBlock content to Anthropic directly when ContentBlocks exist.
Go converts Text/Image/Document/ToolReference blocks without TS-style stripping or sibling-boundary normalization.
OpenAI conversion emits tool output text and then appends structured content as text/image parts, including `[tool:name]` for references.
Responses conversion has the same text-marker fallback for tool references.

gaps.impact: Stale or unsupported tool_reference content can survive into provider requests, and Go misses TS's special handling for tool_reference-adjacent text.

gaps.title: Current Go ToolSearch alignment tests assert non-TS behavior
gaps.description: Several Go tests labeled as TS alignment encode `limit`, min/max clamping, BM25 ranking, score metadata, snippets, and embedding rerank metadata as desired parity. The TS files provided as the benchmark show `max_results`, fixed keyword scoring, and no scores/snippets/rerank fields in the output schema. This gives a false positive on parity and leaves the actual TS behaviors unprotected.

ts_evidence.note: TS schema/output contract uses max_results and typed matches/query/total_deferred_tools.
TS keyword search is a fixed scorer, not BM25.

go_evidence.note: Go alignment tests claim TS exposes `limit` and clamps to [1,50].
Go alignment tests require BM25 ranking and score metadata.
Go alignment tests require snippets/matched text in output.
Go alignment tests require embedding rerank metadata in ToolSearch output.
Basic tests cover structured refs and hints but do not check TS schema, exact-name fast path, MCP prefix fast path, output object shape, or provider gates.

gaps.impact: Future fixes can be blocked by tests that protect Go-specific behavior, and parity regressions can pass because TS-derived cases are absent.

gaps.title: Analytics, read-only metadata, and result-size controls are not aligned with TS
gaps.description: TS ToolSearch logs `tengu_tool_search_outcome` with query, queryType, matchCount, totalDeferredTools, maxResults, and hasMatches; declares itself read-only; and sets maxResultSizeChars to 100000. Go has a ToolSearchOutcomeFn hook but the event omits query/maxResults and is not wired outside tests. Go ToolSearch implements IsConcurrentSafe but no IsReadOnly marker and no ToolSearch-specific maxResultSizeChars metadata/threshold.

ts_evidence.note: TS marks ToolSearch enabled, concurrency-safe, read-only, and maxResultSizeChars 100000.
TS logs structured outcome analytics including query and maxResults.

go_evidence.note: Go ToolSearchOutcomeEvent lacks query/maxResults, and the emitter is only a nil-safe hook.
Go exposes IsConcurrentSafe only.
Outcome tests only assert the hook can emit a partial event and be nil-safe.
Go supports result-size metadata generally, but ToolSearch does not set a TS-equivalent per-tool threshold.

gaps.impact: Operational parity is incomplete: dashboards cannot compare the same dimensions, permission/read-only consumers cannot classify ToolSearch the same way, and result-size behavior depends on global defaults.

candidate_tasks.title: Restore the TS ToolSearch input schema
candidate_tasks.description: Change the model-facing schema from `limit` to TS `max_results`, remove TS-incompatible min/max schema claims unless a true TS bound is added upstream, and make Execute semantics match TS defaulting without advertising Go-only fields.
acceptance: ToolSearch Schema().Properties contains `query` and `max_results` and does not advertise `limit` as the canonical parameter.
`max_results` defaults to 5 when absent, matching TS.
Existing hidden compatibility for `limit` is either removed or explicitly kept behind tests that prove it is not model-facing.
Tests no longer claim TS uses `limit` or [1,50] clamping.

candidate_tasks.title: Align Execute search semantics with TS keyword search
candidate_tasks.description: Make the production Execute path follow the TS searchToolsWithKeywords algorithm: bare exact names, MCP prefix fast path, `select:` multi-select, `+` required terms, fixed scoring weights, and max_results slicing. BM25/cache/embedding helpers can remain only if they do not alter the TS-visible behavior, or should be moved behind non-parity experiments outside ToolSearch.
acceptance: Bare exact deferred and already-loaded tool names return that tool without ranking.
`mcp__server` prefix queries return matching deferred MCP tools before generic keyword scoring.
`+term` required filters use TS name/description/searchHint logic.
Ranking fixtures match TS fixed-weight ordering, including tie behavior where applicable.
Embedding rerank and BM25-specific score/snippet output do not affect ToolSearch parity mode.

candidate_tasks.title: Align ToolSearch output and prompt contract
candidate_tasks.description: Make the Go tool's model-facing description and result mapping match TS: TS query forms, deferred-tool location hint, typed matches/query/total_deferred_tools/pending_mcp_servers data where the Go tool-result abstraction can carry it, success mapped to tool_reference content blocks, and empty-result text compatible with TS.
acceptance: ToolSearch description no longer advertises BM25 scores/snippets as the contract.
Successful Anthropic tool_result content is a list of tool_reference blocks without Go-only score/snippet text mixed into the same structured result.
Empty result text matches TS wording and appends the TS pending-server sentence only when pending_mcp_servers are present.
If Go retains ToolResult metadata for internal observability, provider-bound output remains TS-compatible.

candidate_tasks.title: Implement request-time ToolSearch enablement and visibility gates
candidate_tasks.description: Split optimistic registration from definitive per-request use, mirroring TS. The loop should decide whether ToolSearch is active for each provider request based on env mode, beta kill switch, model support, provider/proxy support, ToolSearch availability after filtering, auto-threshold sizing, and whether there are deferred tools or pending MCP servers.
acceptance: ToolSearch can be registered optimistically but filtered from provider tools when definitive useToolSearch is false.
Deferred tools are hidden only when definitive useToolSearch is true for the request.
Haiku/unsupported model fixtures do not receive ToolSearch or tool_reference-capable results.
Default first-party proxy base URL behavior matches TS unless ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH is explicitly set.
No-deferred/no-pending requests filter ToolSearch out as TS does.

candidate_tasks.title: Add provider-specific defer_loading, beta, and tool_reference normalization
candidate_tasks.description: Represent TS defer_loading in Go tool definitions or prove the provider surface no longer requires it, choose beta headers by provider exactly as TS, and normalize historical tool_reference content before provider conversion when ToolSearch is disabled or references unavailable tools.
acceptance: Go tool definitions can carry defer_loading when useToolSearch and willDefer are true, or an explicit parity decision records why client-side hiding replaces it without changing provider behavior.
Anthropic/Foundry use advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20; Vertex/Bedrock use tool-search-tool-2025-10-19 where applicable.
Tool reference blocks are stripped before provider calls when request-time ToolSearch is disabled.
References to tools no longer registered/available are stripped with a placeholder if all content is removed.
ToolReferenceBlock is never smooshed into mixed tool_result content in a provider-invalid shape.

candidate_tasks.title: Add normal-turn deferred-tools announcements
candidate_tasks.description: Implement the TS normal-turn `deferred_tools_delta` system-reminder flow, including added/removed deferred tools and the same enablement gates. Keep the existing post-compact reminder as recovery state, not as the only announcement path.
acceptance: First active ToolSearch turn announces all currently deferred tool names in a TS-equivalent system reminder.
Subsequent turns announce only added/removed deferred tool deltas.
Announcements are suppressed when ToolSearch is not active for the request.
A fallback `<available-deferred-tools>`-style message is available if the delta path is intentionally disabled.

candidate_tasks.title: Preserve loaded deferred tools through compaction and resume
candidate_tasks.description: Teach Go to extract discovered tools from nested ToolResultBlock.ContentBlocks, store them in compact boundary metadata, and reconstruct QueryLoop.loadedToolNames from existing messages and compact boundary metadata on new/resumed loops.
acceptance: compact.discoveredToolNames finds ToolReferenceBlock values nested inside ToolResultBlock.ContentBlocks.
PreCompactDiscoveredTools contains tools loaded by ToolSearch before full, partial, snip, and session-memory compaction.
New/resumed QueryLoop rebuilds loadedToolNames from current messages and latest compact boundary metadata before building visible definitions.
A post-compact/resume integration test proves a previously loaded deferred tool remains visible without rerunning ToolSearch.

candidate_tasks.title: Wire MCP pending-state and dynamic invalidation into ToolSearch
candidate_tasks.description: Connect ToolSearch's pending/state resolvers to the actual MCP managers used by SetupRegistry, and register list_changed invalidators for the production ToolSearch instance so registry/index state refreshes when dynamic MCP tool lists change.
acceptance: Empty select/keyword misses include pending_mcp_servers when service MCP has pending clients, matching TS output field semantics.
Failed/needs-auth/disabled richer state is either mapped behind TS-compatible pending_mcp_servers output or kept out of provider-visible ToolSearch output.
SetupRegistry wires RegisterMCPListChangedInvalidators for the ToolSearch instance it registers.
A dynamic MCP tools/list_changed integration test proves a stale cached search result is invalidated without manual test-only wiring.

candidate_tasks.title: Replace misleading ToolSearch parity tests with TS-derived goldens
candidate_tasks.description: Rewrite the ToolSearch alignment test suite so it reflects the actual TS files in ../src. Remove or rename tests that intentionally assert Go-only experiments (limit, BM25, score/snippet metadata, embedding rerank) so they do not masquerade as parity coverage.
acceptance: Schema tests assert `max_results` and default 5 from TS.
Search tests cover exact bare names, already-loaded exact names, MCP prefix fast path, select multi-select, required terms, searchHint scoring, and no-match pending_mcp_servers.
Provider tests cover beta stripping/selection and stale/unsupported tool_reference normalization.
Compaction/resume tests cover nested tool_reference extraction and loaded-tool reconstruction.
Any retained BM25/embedding tests are clearly labeled as Go extensions and do not block TS parity.

candidate_tasks.title: Align ToolSearch observability and metadata
candidate_tasks.description: Bring Go operational metadata in line with TS: outcome analytics fields, runtime emitter wiring, read-only classification if the Go permission system supports it, and ToolSearch-specific result-size threshold metadata.
acceptance: ToolSearch outcome events include query, queryType, matchCount, totalDeferredTools, maxResults, and hasMatches.
Outcome event emission is wired to the runtime analytics/logging sink used by other tools, not only unit tests.
ToolSearch has a Go read-only marker or equivalent permission classification consumed by the loop.
ToolSearch results carry a maxResultSizeChars threshold equivalent to TS 100000 where Go's result store consumes it.
